questions.stem: A point $P(3, 2)$ is reflected in the $y$-axis. What are the coordinates of $P'$?
questions.explanation: Reflecting in the $y$-axis changes the sign of the $x$-coordinate while the $y$-coordinate stays the same, giving $(-3, 2)$.

questions.stem: What must you state to fully describe a reflection?

options.text: The equation of the mirror line

questions.explanation: A reflection is fully described by stating the equation of the line of reflection (mirror line).

questions.stem: A shape is reflected in the line $y = x$. The point $(4, 1)$ maps to which point?
questions.explanation: When reflecting in the line $y = x$, the $x$ and $y$ coordinates swap. So $(4, 1)$ becomes $(1, 4)$.

questions.stem: After a reflection, which of the following is true?

options.text: The image is larger than the original
The image has the same orientation as the original
The image has the opposite orientation (laterally inverted)

questions.explanation: A reflection produces a mirror image that is laterally inverted -- the orientation is reversed, but the shape and size remain the same.

questions.stem: A point $Q(5, -3)$ is reflected in the $x$-axis. What are the coordinates of $Q'$?
questions.explanation: Reflecting in the $x$-axis changes the sign of the $y$-coordinate while the $x$-coordinate stays the same, giving $(5, 3)$.

questions.stem: The mirror line for a reflection is always:

options.text: The perpendicular bisector of the line joining each point to its image
Through the centre of the shape
Along one side of the shape

questions.explanation: The mirror line is the perpendicular bisector of the line segment joining any point to its reflected image.

questions.stem: A shape and its image are on opposite sides of the line $x = 2$. What type of transformation has been applied?
questions.explanation: If a shape and its image are on opposite sides of a vertical line and are mirror images, the transformation is a reflection in that line.
